Subject: ClearGlass: Request for sub-100ms p95 & 99.95% uptime — exception review

Team — looping you in on an ask from ClearGlass (enterprise analytics platform). Quick summary: they want a bespoke availability/latency commitment for a pilot of their realtime assist product. Key asks from the customer:

- p95 < 100ms for text-generation flows (main API route)
- 99.95% monthly uptime SLA for the dedicated cluster during pilot (6–12 months)
- Cross-region failover between us-west and us-east for DR

We have the dossier attached (ClearGlass_SLO_request.xlsx) with traffic patterns and peak qps. They are a strategic prospect — exec sponsor, procurement is pushing for firm commitments.

Immediate asks for this thread:
1) Engineering: what are the operational gaps to hit sub-100ms p95 for their expected profile (see sheets: 99th/95th token latencies, burst windows)?
2) Product: can we sign off on a time-limited SLA exception with clear rollback criteria and telemetry requirements?
3) Sales/legal: pricing uplift & contract guardrails.

Can you reply with your top-line assessment today? I'm planning a short sync with ClearGlass tomorrow; want to bring clear asks and constraints.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Quick technical read: thanks for the packet. A few clarifying items we need before we can commit anything operationally:

1) Traffic distribution: what percentage of requests are short-context (<128 tokens) vs long-context (>=1024)? Short-context is much easier to hit sub-100ms.
2) QPS / burst window: their sheet shows 450 qps sustained with 3k burst for 2–5 minutes. Is this correct? If so, we'll need pre-reserved capacity and reserved burst pools.
3) Multi-region: cross-region KV cache coherence is non-trivial. Are they ok with eventual consistency during failover? That impacts observed p95.
4) Model variant: does ClearGlass require a specific model (redwood-llama-13b-qa) or open to a lower-latency distilled variant? Quantized variants can help.

Operational implications (short):
- We'll need a dedicated pool with 2x headroom (reserve + burst) and prefix caching enabled.
- Add a canary routing policy + automatic fallback to a slightly higher-latency model if p95 threatens.
- Instrumentation: we need token-level latency histograms to be emitted to Console (new metric: cg_realtime_p95) for the duration of the pilot.

I'll open ENG-5123 and sketch an implementation plan if you confirm the traffic numbers. Without those, can't sign off.

—Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Folks — appreciate the clear asks. Product standpoint: we can approve a scoped SLA exception but only with the following constraints and acceptance criteria: 

- Scope: only the "realtime assist" API route for up to 3 named production PRDs. No auto-rollout to new routes.
- Term: time-limited pilot, max 12 months with a review at month 3.
- Telemetry: shipping of p50/p95/p99 token latencies and tail error rates to Console (sample rate 100%).
- Operational mitigations required before signing: prefix KV caching enabled, pre-warmed reserved capacity (2x expected sustained QPS), and a documented failover behavior (graceful degraded model fallback).
- Rollback: if sustained p95 breaches >3 incidents in 30 days, SLA reverts to standard terms and customer receives credits.

I'll attach a short conditions doc (availability_conditions.md) that legal and engineering can iterate on. From roadmap perspective we can't commit changes to the serving runtime to support new kernel optimizations specifically for this customer during the pilot. We can prioritize investigation as part of ENG-5123.

—Kimberly
VP, Product — Serving & Runtime
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: ClearGlass exception — internal decision and next steps

Short update and decision log (for deal desk + legal):

Decision: APPROVED (conditional) — Redwood will offer a time-limited SLA exception to ClearGlass for the realtime-assist route with targets of p95 < 100ms and 99.95% monthly uptime, subject to the conditions below.

Conditions (must be delivered before effective date):
- Engineering to enact prefix KV caching and provision dedicated pool with 2x sustained headroom (ENG-5123).
- Console telemetry (cg_realtime_p95) surfaced and exported to customer dashboards; alerts wired to Ops on breach.
- Product & Legal to finalize availability_conditions.md and incorporate rollback triggers into contract.
- Commercial: 25% pricing uplift for the pilot and an SLA credit schedule (to be drafted by Marissa & Legal).
- Term: initial 6-month pilot; auto-extend to 12 months only on mutual written agreement after 90-day review.

Risks / tradeoffs captured: additional reserved capacity increases unit costs; manual on-call and runbook overhead for 90 days. We'll tag spend to the deal and track RAU (reserved allocation utilization) monthly.

Next steps / owners:
- Vivek: open/triage ENG-5123 and provide an implementation ETA by EOD Wed.
- Kimberly: finalize availability_conditions.md and send to Legal.
- Marissa: draft commercial term sheet & initial pricing uplift to present to procurement.
- Vanessa: coordinate customer sync and obtain traffic confirmation.

I'll attach the signed mutual action plan once procurement routes the MPA.

Thanks all — let's keep this tight.

—Vanessa
